title: Reformed mean: sin remains (not imputed) yet true cleansing and inherent justice
source_text: XXII. Atque hoc est quod sibi volunt Theologi Reformati, dum quandoque contendunt peccatum per Christi gratiam, cujus in hac vita participes sumus, non tolli, nec extingui, sed in nobis manere; licet non imputetur, & per Christi meritum & justitiam coram Deo tegatur. Nec enim intelligunt peccatorem, quum justificatur, talem in se manere qualis antea erat, ac in iisdem sordibus volutari, & esse eodem modo peccatis obnoxium; sed solum per Christi mortem & satisfactionem justo quod meretur supplicio eximi. Agnoscunt, ut jam diximus, Deum illos quibus poenam peccatorum condonat a peccati quoque sordibus & maculis mundare, veraque justitia & sanctitate donare, ita ut peccato non amplius serviant, sed membra sua sistant arma justitiae Deo. Verum eorum mens est, peccatum non ita ex fidelibus tolli, quin aliquid peccati in iis reliquum sit, quatenus quotidie in multa peccata labuntur, quorum respectu dicere opus habent in precibus quotidianis, Dimitte nobis debita nostra. Ac praeterea, quoniam etiam in sanctissimis & perfectissimis quibusque manet prava illa concupiscentia, & vitium nobis innatum, quod continuum cum mente bellum gerit, eosque ad malum impellit, & in bene agendo impedit & retardat, motusque repugnantes rationi & legi divinae in iis subinde excitat.
pass_a_gloss: And this is what the Reformed Theologians mean when they sometimes contend that sin through Christ's grace, of which we are partakers in this life, is not taken away nor extinguished, but remains in us; though it is not imputed, and through Christ's merit and righteousness is covered before God. For they do not understand that the sinner, when justified, remains such in himself as he was before, and wallows in the same filth, and is liable to sins in the same way; but only that by Christ's death and satisfaction he is exempted from the just punishment he deserves. They acknowledge, as we have already said, that God cleanses those to whom he remits the penalty of sins also from the filth and stains of sin, and gifts them with true righteousness and holiness, so that they no longer serve sin, but present their members as instruments of righteousness to God. But their mind is that sin is not so taken away from the faithful that something of sin is not left in them, inasmuch as they daily lapse into many sins, with respect to which they need to say in daily prayers, Forgive us our debts. And further, because even in the most holy and perfect there remains that evil concupiscence and inborn vice which wages continual war with the mind, drives them to evil, hinders and slows them in doing well, and now and then stirs in them motions resistant to reason and the divine law.
pass_b_english: When Reformed say sin remains (unimputed, covered), they do not mean the justified stay unrenewed wallowers.
God truly cleanses and gifts inherent justice; yet daily debts and innate concupiscence remain to fight.
